Base directory for this skill: /home/agent/.claude/skills/entire

# Entire CLI

Entire records agent work as **checkpoints** — persistent records tied to commits — and tracks **sessions** across worktrees. This skill covers driving its CLI.

## Rule 1: the CLI documents itself — never guess flags

Entire ships a machine-readable help surface that always matches the installed binary:

```bash
entire agent-help                      # command map + when to use each
entire agent-help <command>            # exact flags for the installed version
entire agent-help <command> <sub>      # drill further
entire agent-help <command> --json     # structured output
```

**Read it before composing any non-trivial invocation.** The CLI evolves quickly; a
flag list memorised in a skill file goes stale, the self-help does not. This file
therefore documents *which command solves which problem* and the traps — command
names are stable, flags are not.

If a command errors on an unknown flag, do not guess a variant. Run
`entire agent-help <command>` and read the real surface.

## Rule 2: never ask the user for the repo

Entire auto-detects the repository from the git `origin` remote. You are already
inside it.

- Pass `--repo` **only** to target a *different* repo than the current one.
- Repo slugs take several forms: `gh/owner/repo` (GitHub-backed), `et/proj/repo`
  (Entire-native), plain `owner/repo`, or a ULID.

`entire agent-help` prints the detected repo in its footer — use that to confirm
which repo you are acting on before any write operation.

## Command map

| Need | Command |
|---|---|
| What did the agent do here? | `checkpoint explain`, `checkpoint list` |
| Find past work by meaning | `checkpoint search` |
| Who/what produced this line? | `why`, `blame` |
| Which agent knows this area? | `experts` |
| Session state, stop, resume | `session` |
| Activity summary | `recap`, `activity` |
| Written summary of recent work | `dispatch` |
| Is Entire on? | `status`, `enable`, `disable` |
| Something is stuck | `doctor` |
| Remove local session data | `clean` |
| Settings (telemetry, hooks, backend) | `configure` |
| Install agent hooks | `agent add/remove/list` |
| Raw API call | `api` |
| Orgs / projects / repos / access | `org`, `project`, `repo`, `grant` |
| Auth | `login`, `logout`, `auth` |
| Experimental workflows | `labs` |

## Provenance — the highest-value commands

These answer questions plain git cannot, because they join commits to the prompts
and sessions that produced them.

```bash
entire why <file>:42            # commit + checkpoint + prompt + session behind a line
entire blame <file>:12-20       # git-blame enriched with checkpoint metadata
entire blame <file> --long      # adds agent, model, author, session columns
entire experts <scope-or-query> # rank agent provenance for a code scope
entire experts --staged         # use staged paths as the scope
```

All three accept `--json`. Reach for `entire why` before speculating about *why*
code looks a certain way — it often returns the literal prompt that produced it.

## Search

```bash
entire checkpoint search "fix login"          # hybrid semantic + keyword, current repo
entire checkpoint search "..." --all-repos    # widen scope
entire checkpoint search "..." --code         # search code content instead
entire checkpoint search "..." --json --limit 20
```

Queries support inline filters: `author:<name>`, `date:<week|month>`,
`branch:<name>`, `repo:<owner/name>`, `repo:*`.

Requires `entire login` (GitHub device flow). Run with no arguments for an
interactive picker — **avoid that in an agent context**, pass a query and `--json`.

## Reading a checkpoint

```bash
entire checkpoint list                     # checkpoints on the current branch
entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>         # auto-detects checkpoint ID vs commit SHA
entire checkpoint explain <id> --short     # summary only
entire checkpoint explain <id> --json      # metadata only; never embeds transcript bytes
entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript # stream raw JSONL transcript to stdout
```

Checkpoint IDs may be abbreviated to any unambiguous prefix. A commit carrying an
`Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer resolves as a positional target too.

`--json` and `--transcript` are deliberately separate surfaces: metadata never
carries transcript bytes. If you need both, make two calls.

## Sessions

```bash
entire session current            # active session for this worktree
entire session list               # across all worktrees
entire session info <id> --json
entire session stop               # interactive without an id
entire session resume <branch>
entire session adopt <id> --from ../other-worktree
```

## Token usage

```bash
entire checkpoint tokens <id>                      # usage + optimization advice
entire checkpoint tokens <id> --agent-brief         # compact next-step guidance for agents
entire checkpoint tokens <id> --compare <baseline>  # qualify a reduction
entire session tokens <id>
entire tokens profile                               # aggregate across checkpoints (labs)
```

`--agent-brief` is the right output mode when *you* are the consumer.

## Reporting

```bash
entire recap --week --view both     # day (default) | week | month | 90
entire recap --static               # non-interactive — required in agent context
entire activity                     # overview + recent sessions
entire activity --commits           # recent commits instead
entire dispatch --since 7d          # written summary of recent agent work
entire dispatch --local --all-branches
```

`recap` opens an interactive TUI by default. **Always pass `--static`** when you
are not a human at a terminal.

## Labs (experimental — surface may change)

```bash
entire review                       # multi-agent review of the branch, judge consolidates
entire review --list                # configured profiles
entire investigate <seed-doc>       # multi-agent investigation to quorum
entire investigate show <run-id>
entire import claude-code           # import Claude Code transcripts as read-only history
```

`entire review` is user-triggered and spawns real agents. Do not launch it on your
own initiative — surface it as a suggestion and let the user decide.

## Traps

**Interactive by default.** `recap`, `checkpoint search` with no query,
`session stop` with no id, `review --configure`, and `experts --tui` open TUIs
that will hang a non-interactive session. Pass `--static`, `--json`, or an explicit
argument. `ACCESSIBLE=1` in the environment swaps TUIs for plain-text prompts and
is a useful fallback.

**`entire clean` deletes work.** It removes session state and shadow branches.
Always `--dry-run` first; treat `--force --all` as destructive and confirm with the
user before running it.

**`entire investigate --issue-link` needs `--allow-untrusted-seed`** to run
non-interactively, because a GitHub issue is attacker-influenced content and the
agents run with permission bypass. That guard exists for a reason — do not add the
flag reflexively to silence the refusal.

**Pushes carry a second branch.** `git push` also pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1`.
A remote `HEAD` may resolve to that branch rather than `main`, which makes web UIs
appear to show "nothing" for the project. Check with `git ls-remote origin`.

**`entire api` is a real authenticated call.** `--to core` hits the control plane,
`--to cell` your home cell. Method defaults to GET, but becomes POST as soon as a
field or body is supplied — an accidental `-F` turns a read into a write. Path
placeholders `{owner}`, `{repo}`, `{repo_id}` are filled from the origin remote.

## Setup and repair

```bash
entire enable --agent claude-code   # non-interactive hook install
entire enable --agent-help-skill    # install Entire's own official agent-help skill
entire agent list                   # installed + available agents
entire status --detailed --json
entire doctor                       # diagnose stuck sessions, disconnected metadata branches
entire doctor --force               # auto-fix without prompting
entire configure --telemetry=false
```

`doctor` covers three known failure modes: metadata branches that share no common
ancestor with their remote, Codex hooks missing a trust hash, and sessions stuck in
ACTIVE (idle > 1h) or ENDED (uncondensed) phase.

Note that Entire ships an official `--agent-help-skill`. If a repo installs it,
prefer it as the authority for that repo and keep this skill for cross-repo habits.

13	// The clone list is the item level of a clone run (D3).
14	//
15	// It used to keep its own five states, its own rows, its own index and its own
16	// spinner frame — a fifth bookkeeping beside the four internal/jobs replaced,
17	// and the one the plan named as the prototype to generalise. Those five states
18	// are where jobs.ItemState came from, so the mapping is direct:
19	//
20	//	queued        → ItemQueued
21	//	cloning       → ItemRunning
22	//	cloned        → ItemDone
23	//	already there → ItemSkipped
24	//	failed        → ItemFailed
25	//
26	// What this screen is now is a **rendering** of the run: the rows are the
27	// snapshot's items, in the order the walk found them, and the frame is the
28	// router's (D5). Nothing here is authoritative, which is what lets `:jobs` show
29	// the same run without either copy drifting from the other.
30	
31	// cloneRow is one target of the run, with the shared frame stamped on.
32	//
33	// The frame rides on the row because the columns are built once and close over
34	// nothing — the same reason jobsview has runRow. It is text rather than a
35	// rendered spinner because a table cell must carry no escape sequence
36	// (Rule 122).
37	type cloneRow struct {
38		item  jobs.Item
39		frame string
40	}
41	
42	// cloneList is the ModeCloning screen: the run in flight and the table showing
43	// it. It is the progress view and the report both — decision 9 leaves modals
44	// for yes/no confirmations only.
45	type cloneList struct {
46		table datatable.Model[cloneRow]
47	
48		// run is the last snapshot of this screen's run. It is a copy, replaced
49		// whole on every broadcast — there is nothing to reconcile, which is what
50		// removed the index and the upsert.
51		run    jobs.Run
52		target string
53	
54		// events is the pipeline's channel, and the only thing this struct still
55		// owns. It is not state: it is what waitForCloneEvent blocks on.
56		events <-chan cloneEvent
57	
58		// cancelling is set by `esc` and cleared by nothing: a run that is stopping
59		// cannot be restarted, only awaited. A second `esc` must not force, because
60		// forcing is the half-cloned directory decision 12 avoids.
61		//
62		// It is kept here rather than read back from the run for one frame's worth
63		// of honesty: `esc` asks the router, and the answer arrives in the next
64		// broadcast. Without it the key would look ignored until then.
65		cancelling bool
66	}

70		colClonePathMin   = 30
71		colCloneDetailMin = 20
72	)

75	// position it happens to sit at today.

77		colCloneRepository = iota
78		colCloneDetail
79		colCloneStatus

82	func newCloneList(target string, events <-chan cloneEvent) *cloneList {
83		return &cloneList{

87				Columns: cloneColumns(),
88				// Discovery order, deliberately: it is the order things happened, and
89				// a list that reorders itself while it fills is unreadable. `.` still
90				// sorts on demand.
91				SortColumn: -1,
92			}),
93		}
94	}

96	// cloneColumns describes the clone list.
97	//
98	// The repository comes first and the status last. The rows are one long list of
99	// paths under a common prefix, so the name is what the eye runs down to find a
100	// line; a status column on the left pushes every one of them right by sixteen
101	// cells and puts the changing text where the stable text should be.
102	func cloneColumns() []datatable.Column[cloneRow] {
103		return []datatable.Column[cloneRow]{
104			{
105				Title: "Repository", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: colClonePathMin, Flex: 2, TruncateHead: true,
106				Cell:   func(r cloneRow) string { return r.item.Name() },
107				Less:   func(a, b cloneRow) bool { return strings.ToLower(a.item.Name()) < strings.ToLower(b.item.Name()) },
108				Search: func(r cloneRow) string { return r.item.Name() },
109			},
110			{
111				Title: "Detail", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, Optional: true, MinWidth: colCloneDetailMin, Flex: 1,
112				Cell:   func(r cloneRow) string { return r.item.Detail },
113				Search: func(r cloneRow) string { return r.item.Detail },
114			},
115			{
116				Title: "Status", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: colCloneStatusMin,
117				Cell:  cloneStatusLabel,
118				Style: cloneStatusStyle,
119				Less:  func(a, b cloneRow) bool { return a.item.State < b.item.State },
120			},
121		}
122	}
123	
124	// cloneStatusLabel is the status cell: an icon and a word, plain text.
125	//

127	// means here, where a sync's skip means something else entirely. The state is
128	// shared, the wording is the view's — the same split Reporter draws.
129	func cloneStatusLabel(r cloneRow) string {
130		switch r.item.State {
131		case jobs.ItemRunning:
132			return r.frame + " cloning"
133		case jobs.ItemDone:
134			return theme.IconOK + " cloned"
135		case jobs.ItemSkipped:
136			return theme.IconSkipped + " already there"
137		case jobs.ItemFailed:
138			return theme.IconError + " failed"
139		default:

141		}
142	}

145	//
146	// The five states are the whole vocabulary of this screen, and they are the one
147	// thing a run of forty rows is read for: which ones failed, which are still
148	// going, which were already on disk and were left alone.
149	func cloneStatusStyle(r cloneRow) lipgloss.Style {
150		switch r.item.State {
151		case jobs.ItemDone:
152			return theme.StatusOKStyle
153		case jobs.ItemFailed:
154			return theme.StatusErrorStyle
155		case jobs.ItemRunning:

157		default: // queued, and already there — neither is news
158			return theme.DimStyle
159		}

162	// setRun replaces the screen's copy of the run and rebuilds the table.

165	// because it belongs to the list and not to any repository: one spinner, on

174			}
175			items[i] = row
176		}
177		l.table.SetItems(items)
178	}
179	
180	// finished reports whether the run has settled: the walk sealed, and every
181	// target done with.
182	func (l *cloneList) finished() bool { return l.run.Finished() }
183	
184	// running counts the clones still in flight, which is what `esc` has to wait
185	// for and what the view states while it does.
186	func (l *cloneList) running() int {
187		n := 0
188		for _, item := range l.run.Items {

194	}

205	// the view is still alive.

207		var out []string

230		}
231		return jobs.Run{}, false

Oui — et le code plaide déjà pour, plus fort que je ne l'avais vu. Quatre points :

**1. `delete` est déjà un kind de job.** `jobs.KindDelete` existe, et la doc de `Run.Stoppable()` raisonne explicitement dessus : *"A delete falls through all four while it runs: one item, in flight, of a kind that must never be cut."* Sauf que seul `workspaces` l'utilise (suppression d'un répertoire local). Le delete de l'explorer — celui qui est réellement un appel réseau — n'est pas enregistré. C'est l'incohérence.

**2. Mon implémentation avait un vrai bug que les jobs corrigent.** J'allais estampiller la frame de `m.spinner` sur la ligne optimiste. Mais `handleSpinnerTick` (update.go:210) sort immédiatement si `!m.loading` — après un submit l'arbre ne charge pas, donc le spinner resterait sur la frame zéro, ce qui se lit comme un blocage. C'est exactement la panne que D5 a supprimée pour les lignes de clone : elles prennent la frame du routeur via le broadcast, *"so a clone keeps turning whether or not this view is on screen — and cannot freeze on frame zero if this chain dies."* L'explorer reçoit déjà `jobs.ChangedMsg` ; `msg.Frame` est gratuit.

**3. « On ne peut rien faire sur cette ligne » est déjà écrit.** `busy()` + `busyMessage` dans workspaces, qui répondent depuis le registre — donc voient le travail lancé depuis *n'importe quelle* vue. Le refaire localement, c'est reconstruire la quatrième comptabilité que la doc du paquet `jobs` s'ouvre en décrivant.

**4. Ça ferme un bug de contexte au passage.** `handleProjectCreated` appelle `handleRefresh()` sans condition : si le contexte change pendant que le POST est en vol, on rafraîchit l'arbre du nouveau contexte. `Run.Context` est estampillé au lancement précisément pour ça — c'est la famille de D68 (commit cd62621).

**Plan révisé :**
- `KindCreate` ajouté — il faut répondre à `Cancellable()` (non : un POST ne se dé-envoie pas, et le demi-créé est déjà le cas `TemplateError`) et à `Verb()` (`"Creating"`). `TestEveryKindAnswersWhetherItCanBeCancelled` compte les kinds et échouera tant que la table D7 n'est pas à jour.
- Explorer : create **et** delete passent par `jobs.StartInContext`, cible = `parent/slug` (connue au submit) et `node.FullPath`.
- La frame vient du broadcast, plus de `m.spinner` sur les lignes.
- Garde `busy()` locale à l'explorer sur le modèle de workspaces + grisage Rule 130 avec motif nommé.

**Ce que les jobs ne donnent pas**, et qu'il faut quand même écrire : la ligne optimiste elle-même. Le registre suit le travail, il ne pose pas de nœud dans l'arbre — le `TreeNode` placeholder (`Creating: true`) reste à la charge de la vue. C'est la moitié de mon plan initial qui survit.

### Long-running work reports without taking the screen

A scan, a sync or a delete outlives the moment the user spends looking at the
view that started it. Its progress messages are therefore addressed **by name**
to that view — `routeToView(target, msg)` in `app.go` — and never to the view on
screen, and routing one never changes `currentView`.

Three properties, and each is load-bearing:

| | |
|---|---|
| The owning view is updated | it holds the row's marker, its footer state and its cache write; a message dropped because the user walked away leaves the row marked busy for the life of the view |
| The active view is *not* | it would act on progress that is not its own |
| `currentView` is untouched | `handleWorkspaceScanComplete` used to set it on every finished repository, so a batch of twelve made every other view unusable until the last one landed (D67) |

The router does not re-measure the layout on these, unlike
`forwardToActiveView`: a view the user is not looking at cannot change the
footer's shape on screen, and it is measured on its way back in — `switchView`
asks for a resize.

Making the marker survive re-entry is what makes the routing safe: `setEntries`
deliberately does not touch `scanningPaths`, so the reload `Init` triggers on
the way back in leaves in-flight work alone.

### The jobs registry — `internal/jobs`

One bookkeeping of everything long-running, owned by the router
(`App.jobs`). Before it there were four, and none could see the others:
`workspaces` kept three maps of paths, `oci_resources` a map of image names, the
security inventory a flag per row, and the clone screen five states per
repository. A scan started from `:sec` was therefore invisible to the `busy()`
guard in `ws`, and the two wrote the same cache entry.

Two levels: a **`Run`** is one batch started in one go from one view, and holds
an **`Item`** per target. `RunState` is *derived* from the items and never
stored — a field would be a second answer to a question the items already
answer, and the two drift the first time a transition is missed.

| | |
|---|---|
| `Start(run)` | admits a batch, from `Update` and never from a `Cmd` (Rule 110). Every launch site knows its full target list when it dispatches, which is what makes "8 waiting" sayable |

| `Attach` / `AttachRun` | store a `context.CancelFunc`; it arrives in the message that says the item started, because the context is created inside the `Cmd` |
| `Cancel(id)` | stops the queue always; cuts work in flight only where that leaves nothing behind (`Kind.Cancellable`) |
| `Snapshot()` | a **copy**, cancel functions cleared |
| `Running()` | runs that have not settled |

`C` in the explorer opens a **selection mode** over the same tree, and `enter`

pas (Rule 128).

`pendingSelectPath` et `expandToPath` sont supprimés avec leurs quatre tests :
ils existaient pour retrouver la ressource créée après le refresh, et il n'y a
plus de refresh. La propriété qu'ils protégeaient — le curseur finit sur ce
qu'on vient de créer — est réassertée sur le nouveau mécanisme.
